### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/service-storage`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **19** documentable anchor(s).

**18** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 296e2ec86cf8d55ee19e0546fb8cb5c64bb92076`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **178** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 296e2ec86cf8d55ee19e0546fb8cb5c64bb92076` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9c92d1e8b7739347e18ba8f10829bf4f4038bea8` — the merge of head `5bd8b5dc34a076a1f24fdb2190743c3526d666e8` into base `296e2ec86cf8d55ee19e0546fb8cb5c64bb92076`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9c92d1e8b7739347e18ba8f10829bf4f4038bea8 && git checkout 9c92d1e8b7739347e18ba8f10829bf4f4038bea8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 296e2ec86cf8d55ee19e0546fb8cb5c64bb92076 5bd8b5dc34a076a1f24fdb2190743c3526d666e8 && git checkout -B drift-repro 296e2ec86cf8d55ee19e0546fb8cb5c64bb92076 && git merge --no-ff 5bd8b5dc34a076a1f24fdb2190743c3526d666e8

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 296e2ec86cf8d55ee19e0546fb8cb5c64bb92076
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 296e2ec86cf8d55ee19e0546fb8cb5c64bb92076` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5bd8b5dc34a076a1f24fdb2190743c3526d666e8`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts + packages/services/service-storage/src/record-file-access.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-routes.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-service-plugin.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/file-attachment-service.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/upload-link-page.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts

PR #32779 for card #32734. Read: the card body and its five comments (6825300215, 6828174337, 6828316677, 6828583188, 6829977284), sub-issue #32768 (no comments), the PR body, its ten-file list, the net diff against `main`, and the check-runs on this head. The two test files, the changeset prose and the docs are the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

No must-fix. One should-fix (S1) and three nits (N1 to N3), all in ④. Three check-runs on this head are red and two are still running; they are listed in ③ and are the seat's to clear before landing.

### ① Derived judgments

The PR declares `Clause-②: no` with no arm. Judged right. Every change the diff implies:

1. **Ledger row.** `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER['@objectstack/service-storage']` gains `RECORD_LOCKED`. Right, and no widening. The code is already a member of `RegisteredErrorCode` and `ErrorCode` through the `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` row, so the union, `REGISTERED_ERROR_CODES` and `ApiErrorSchema.code` accept exactly what they accepted. The generated reference lists the deduped union and does not move. The ledger's own header states the rule: a per-package row is provenance, not identity, and what widens the face is registering a code the union does not hold. `Type Check · consumer gates` (it runs `check:api-surface`) and `Lint · docs & code guards` (it runs `check:error-code-provenance`) both concluded success, with no snapshot in the diff.
2. **`create_upload_link` and `createUploadLinkAs`, field target.** Two new refusals: `403 FIELD_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` for a `readonly: true` field, `409 RECORD_LOCKED` for a record a pending approval locks. Right, as a declared precondition enforced and not a declared capability removed. The input schema is unchanged, and `FIELD_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` was already this door's answer. `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx` on `main` already says the tool "needs a record the caller may edit (and, for a field, a field they may write)". A link to a static `readonly` field could never attach: the engine hides the caller's value from the hooks and then strips it for every non-system writer, and a link is spent with `isSystem: false`. A link to a locked record attached only when the approval was decided inside the link's ten minutes. That one sequence is now refused at issue, which is the card's first Expected item. No `(narrowing)` arm is owed: no published key, value, export or schema is narrowed, and a consumer has nothing to migrate.
3. **`PUT /storage/upload-links/:token`.** `403 FIELD_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` where the door answered `200` with the field unchanged. `409 RECORD_LOCKED`, and `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` for the validation shape, where it answered `500 INTERNAL`. Any other throw carrying a string code and a 4xx declared as `statusCode` is relayed as well. Right: one false success and two mis-statused refusals corrected. The success body is unchanged and each of those codes is already in the declared vocabulary.
4. **Upload page.** "Attached" now needs `success === true` and `data.fileId`. Right. It is a browser page, not a published surface.
5. **`create_upload_link` description** (`packages/mcp`). Prose on a published tool; no name or schema moves. Right for clause ②. Its accuracy is S1 in ④.
6. **`getApprovals`** on `RecordFileAccessDeps` and `FileAttachmentServiceDeps`. Optional, and neither interface is reachable from the package entry (`src/index.ts` exports only `ICallerFileAttachmentService` from that module). No public surface.

`Metadata-protocol: none` is right. Nothing an author can write changes: `readonly`, `readonlyWhen` and `lockRecord` keep their meaning and are enforced at one more door.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/service-storage`, `@objectstack/mcp` and `@objectstack/spec`. Matches: those are the three published packages whose `src` the diff moves, and `@objectstack/dogfood` is private. `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`. The changeset carries both declaration lines, and they equal the PR body's and the claim's. No BREAKING carrier is owed (① item 2). `Check Changeset` concluded success.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report 6829977284: `open_questions` is empty, `security_findings` reads `none`, `out_of_scope_findings` is empty. Its six deviations:

1. Branch `claude/project-thread-4bhuy8` instead of the claim's. Recorded by amendment 6828316677, but the gate does not read that amendment as a claim: `PR-body guards (claim · duplicate · Part-of · single-writer path)` concluded failure on this head, "PR #32779 closes #32734 with no `Claim:` on the card naming `claude/project-thread-4bhuy8`". Escalated to the seat. It is a red check, not a contract finding.
2. File surface extended to the ledger row, with a spec patch. Answered by amendment 6828583188. It falls inside the spec lane's pre-approved ledger-append class (an existing code, the appender's own package section, a pure addition), and this record is the contract review that class still owes. The report cites a "ruling Q1=A" and "Q2=A"; no comment on the card carries those letters, and amendment 6828583188 is where both outcomes are written.
3. One sentence of the tool description. Inside the declared surface; see S1.
4. Optional `getApprovals` dep. Inside the declared surface; ① item 6.
5. The relay now answers the validation shape `400`. Accepted as the same defect class (④). It is stated in the PR's Acceptance notes only and no test pins it. For the seat's ACCEPT.
6. No assignee on `pr_create`. Process, the seat's.

The issue-time `readonlyWhen` half is carried by #32768 (open, `Blocked-by` this card). Its premise is checked in ④.

Check-runs on this head at 2026-11-12T17:12Z, 66 in all: 50 success, 11 skipped, 3 failure, 2 in progress.

- Failure: `PR-body guards` (deviation 1 above).
- Failure: `Test UI (16/16)` and its aggregate `Test UI`. The failing test is `ui/packages/plugin-dashboard/src/__tests__/DashboardRenderer.datasetBatch-32165.test.tsx`, "Network escape: this test reached a REAL socket". The diff touches no path under `ui/`. Whether `main` carries the same signature was not read here; it is the seat's reading before landing.
- In progress: `Test Core (3/8)` and `Test Core (8/8)`.
- The dogfood shards do not run on a pull request, by `ci.yml`'s design. The dogfood pin's only reading on this head is the dev's local run.

A security item was raised to the seat privately.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts`** (the `hits` file). Holds. Each clause of the row's comment is true of the tree:

- The stamp site is `refuse('RECORD_LOCKED', 409, …)` in the field branch of `createUploadLinkAs`.
- It asks `IApprovalService.getRecordLock` (an optional member answering `{ locked }` or `null`) before the link row is written.
- The code's other row is `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, whose record-lock hook throws it with `statusCode: 409`.
- The upload-link door relays that throw with its status, code and message.

The row sits in alphabetical order and follows the second-emitter precedent of `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`, the row above it. Accepted against the card's "pending (approval lock)" row.

**`record-file-access.ts`**. Agrees with the contract.

- Mint and hook ask one judgement. `getRecordLock` calls `recordHeldByLockingApproval`, which uses the same pending-request lookup and the same `nodeConfigLocksRecord` the hook uses for a by-id write. The hook's three write-side exemptions cannot apply to a link's write: it is never `isSystem`, carries no `flowRunId`, and a file field is not the status mirror. So a record the mint refuses is one the hook would refuse.
- "A `readonly` field takes no value from a user's write" is true. `engine-update.ts` hides the caller's static `readonly` values from the hooks, and `stripReadonlyFields` takes them out for every non-system caller.
- "No judgement a door can ask without writing", said of `readonlyWhen`, is true. `engine-validate.ts` states that the preview does not run `readonlyWhen`, and the row-write probe names conditional read-only and the approval lock among what it does not cover.
- On use, the strict refusal is thrown after the `beforeUpdate` hooks and before the driver. A lock therefore answers `409` first and a holding `readonlyWhen` answers `403`. No `afterUpdate` runs, so nothing is claimed and a single-file field's previous file is not released.
- `discard` is the first statement of the `catch` and swallows its own faults, so it runs on every refusal in the block. The link row is deleted in `finally`.
- `readonlyRefusalOf` words every drop other than `readonly_when` as read-only. That is the only other reason a payload of one file field can meet.
- Where `getRecordLock` is absent, the door mints as before and the hook refuses on use. The contract's "a door answers `501`, never a guess" binds a door that answers the lock question. This one answers none, and the dep's docblock says what happens.

**`storage-routes.ts`**. Agrees; see N2 and N3. The new reading is a superset of the old one, with `status` still read first. I tried to make it relay a sentence not meant for the link's holder and found none:

- Of the in-repo producers that declare `statusCode` alone, the only one a link's by-id, single-row, user write can reach is the lock hook's per-record sentence. The hook already narrows the record title in that sentence by the writer's own field visibility, and the page is served only to that writer. Its three operator sentences need a multi-id or predicate write.
- `ValidationError`'s message is composed for verbatim display.
- A throw with no string `code`, such as an unevaluable hook condition, still falls to `500`.

**`upload-link-page.ts`**. Agrees. The PUT door has one success body, `{ fileId, size, field | attachmentId }`. `fileId` is always present: `randomUUID()` for a field, and for an attachment the `AttachedFile.fileId` that `attachFileAs` returns, a required member of that contract. Both targets therefore read as attached. The message is set through `textContent`, so a relayed record title cannot become markup. The card's false success carried `data.fileId`, so the strict write is what closes it; this predicate only stops a 2xx without the declared body from reading as attached.

**`storage-service-plugin.ts`, `file-attachment-service.ts`**. Agree. `ctx.getService('approvals')` is late-bound, under the name `plugin-approvals` registers, and answers `null` when absent. It is the same shape as `plugin-sharing`'s probe of that service.

**`packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts`**. One sentence disagrees with the code.

- **S1, should-fix.** "a record a pending approval locks, or a read-only field, gets no link" is true of a `field` target only. The lock check sits in the field branch. `attachments: true` on a locked record still mints and still attaches: the PR body says so, and nothing on the `sys_attachment` insert asks the lock. The description covers both targets and is what an agent reads when it decides whether to offer an upload, so as written it tells the agent that a locked record cannot take an attachment. "A read-only field" likewise means the `readonly` declaration only: a field read-only through `readonlyWhen` still gets a link until #32768. The sentence should say which target and which declaration.

Nits:

- **N1.** The relayed lock sentence reaches the page with its code prefix, `RECORD_LOCKED: …`. The `/api/v1/data` door, whose reading of the same throw the PR body cites, strips a producer's own code prefix before the sentence reaches a person (`withoutDeclaredCodePrefix`). The strict refusal's sentence also names the object and the field by API name. Both are page copy, and #32712 is the card on that page's wording.
- **N2.** `relayUploadLinkRefusal` resolves the throw and still puts the thrown spelling in `error.code` under a cast. `relayAttachFailure` in the same file answers the resolver's closed `code` with `demotedDeclaredCode` beside it, which is the #9106 ruling (a closed vocabulary at every door). The cast is on `main` already for the `status` spelling. This diff extends it to `statusCode`, and no producer reachable today carries an unregistered code. A follow-up card.
- **N3.** The docblock on `relayUploadLinkRefusal` names two spellings. `declaredStatus` has a third limb, the validation shape. The comment should say what the PR's Acceptance notes say.
